# rsTerrain · Terrain Mesh

> Module: Terrain / Analysis & Simulation

[← Back to command index](/en/commands/)

**Function**: The terrain mesh (Mesh) generated by Delaunay triangulation of contour lines is output by overlapping with the original contour lines.

![rsTerrain result comparison: the left side is the contour line draft display, and the right side is the terrain mesh surface (entity display) generated by Delaunay triangulation of the same set of contour lines.](../../assets/rsTerrain/image1.png)
*rsTerrain result comparison (line draft contour on the left + Delaunay terrain mesh surface on the right)*

> Screenshots and videos may show a Chinese-language interface. Labels and control positions can vary by Rhino or RSTool version.

**Run**: Enter `rsTerrain` in the Rhino command line (command-line interaction).

**Workflow**:

1. Command line input rsTerrain
2. Select a group of contour lines (curves/polylines, you can select multiple lines)
3. Command line input sampling length samplingLength (default 5.0, scaled by current model units)
4. Generate terrain mesh (Mesh) output from contour Delaunay triangulation

**Parameters**:

| Display name | Parameter | Type | Default | Range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Sample length | samplingLength | double | 5.0 | Scale by current model units, >0 | Static default value lastDivLength=5, which will be converted according to model units; the smaller the value, the denser the grid. |

**Notes**: The command is command line interaction (no Eto dialog box), and the process is fixed as: select contour → prompt for sampling length → direct network output.

Mesh construction algorithm: takes discrete points sampled according to the sampling length on the contour line as input, and uses Delaunay triangulation to generate the surface mesh; the output is a Rhino Mesh entity, which is juxtaposed with the original contour layer. It can be viewed by switching the line draft/entity/rendering mode in the viewport.

Sampling length samplingLength: determines the grid density between contours. This value will be converted according to the current model unit (millimetre map, centimeter map, and meter map have different scaling). The smaller the value, the denser the points and the finer the grid, but the calculation amount will increase; too small will cause the model to be too large and stuck. It is generally recommended to first use the default value of 5.0 to get the general terrain, and then adjust it to 2.0–3.0 to add fine valley saddles and other subtle undulations depending on the accuracy.

Input requirements: At least 3 valid vertices/points are required to construct a mesh (Delaunay's minimum requirement); contours must be closed or semi-closed curves. Broken lines will trigger an internal max=0 error in the command and prompt "The sampling length must be greater than zero"; contour objects (such as Mesh, Brep) must be converted to contours or grids with their own elevation points before running this command, otherwise the sampling will fail due to no vertex.

Connect with upstream and downstream commands: The output Mesh of this command is the standard input source for rsTerrainAnalysis terrain analysis and rsTerrainEdit terrain editing; before doing terrain analysis, you usually use this command to get the mesh, and then use rsEarth to pull terrain data as a supplementary reference.
